description:
FILED s429 (Fable), found by the #259 matrix (its one-line sub declarations).  PRE-EXISTING.
Six-probe bisect (runpcl, s429):

  q1 use feature "signatures"; no warnings; sub f ($x, @r) { "[@r]" }\nprint f(0), "\n";   -> WARNS, then []
  q2 same with `sub f($x, @r)` (no space)                                               -> WARNS
  q5 use feature "signatures"; sub f ($x, @r) { "[@r]" }\n...                           -> WARNS  (no `no warnings` at all)
  q6 no warnings; use feature "signatures"; sub f ($x, @r) {...}\n...                   -> WARNS
  q3 use feature "signatures"; no warnings;\nsub f ($x, @r) {...}\n...                  -> silent
  q4 use feature "signatures";\nno warnings;\nsub f ($x, @r) {...}\n...                 -> silent

So the trigger is the `sub` sharing the LINE with `use feature "signatures"`; `no warnings`
is irrelevant.  Output is right ([]), only the warning is spurious â perl never warns on
joining an empty array, and warnings are not even enabled.  Two candidate causes, measure
which: (a) the signatures-feature region is computed by LINE, so a sub on the pragma's own
line is treated as outside it and its `($x, @r)` is lowered by the prototype/old path
(look at the emitted p-sub: q5 vs q3 should differ), or (b) the `no warnings`/`use
warnings` region is line-based and the body lands under an enabled 'uninitialized'
category that then mis-fires on an empty array join.  Compare `./pl2cl` emission of q5
and q3 first â it is a 2-minute discriminator.  Low priority (one-line pragma+sub is
rare in real code; the matrix generator wrote it that way).


=== s438e (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE.  Cause (a) of the two this task named, and
the 2-minute discriminator it prescribed answered it: `./pl2cl` on q5 vs q3
emits `(p-sub pl-f ($x &rest @r) â¦)` for the one-line spelling and
`(p-sub pl-f (&rest %_args) (p-args-body (p-check-arity â¦) (let* (($x â¦)
(@r (p-sig-rest-array @_ 1))) â¦)))` for the multi-line one.  So the one-line
sub took the OLD-PROTOTYPE path: the params became a raw CL lambda list, and
the empty slurpy `@r` -- a raw rest list, not a p-array -- interpolated as an
uninitialized value.  Output was right either way; only the warning was
spurious, exactly as reported.

THE FEATURE REGION IS PPI'S, NOT PCL'S: `Pl::Parser::_sub_head` set
`$is_signature_syntax` only for a `PPI::Structure::Signature`, and PPI lexes
`($x, @r)` that way only when the feature is in force -- which its tracking
starts at the line AFTER the pragma.  On the pragma's own line the identical
text arrives as a `PPI::Token::Prototype` and the flag stayed 0.

THE REPAIR IS THE BOUNDARY, NOT THE TEXT, and that distinction was MEASURED,
not reasoned: a first attempt made the flag purely textual (named params =>
signature) and corpus-diff caught it -- perl-tests/signatures.t:17 has
`sub t000 ($a) { $a || "z" }` where the feature is NOT yet on (it arrives at
line 32) and asserts `&t000(456) == 123`, i.e. perl reads `($a)` as an old-style
prototype there.  So `_sub_head` now sets the flag for a Token::Prototype only
when it has named params AND `_signatures_enabled_at($stmt)` -- an enabling
pragma (`use feature`/`use experimental` naming signatures, or a `use v5.36`+
bundle) at an earlier LINE, or the same line at an earlier COLUMN.  It is
deliberately not a lexical scope walk: it exists to recover PPI's one missing
line, and PPI owns every other position.

RULE 11: the textual "named params" test existed in FOUR copies -- _sub_head's
absence of one, parse_prototype_or_signature, Parser2's _is_pure_prototype and
_signature_param_canons (added by #454 the same day).  It is now ONE function,
`Pl::Parser::proto_text_has_named_params`, and all of them ask it.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over the 111 (the textual attempt moved
signatures.t; the boundary version does not); emission-ab over lib/**.pm +
cpan-tests/** + perl's own t/ = 951 files SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF; gate and
full sweep with #454 in the same batch.  Guard: two rows in
Pl/t/sig-param-shadow-01.t (the pragma's own line; and a comment recording the
negative the file deliberately does NOT assert).

RESIDUE, filed as #486 and PRE-EXISTING (blessed in docs/fail-baseline.tsv):
an old-style prototype with NAMES binds its names as parameters on BOTH paths,
so `sub t000 ($a)` outside a signature region answers 456 where perl answers
123.  Choosing between the two lowering paths cannot fix that; the
old-prototype path must stop binding.
subject: `use feature "signatures"; sub f ($x, @r) {...}` on ONE LINE: interpolating the empty slurpy `"@r"` warns "Use of uninitialized value in join or string" (perl silent) â the feature region looks LINE-based
